items.reason: The worker unconditionally completes failed offsets in finally, allowing failed messages to be committed and skipped.

This describes terminate() failing to join the commit thread, allowing an in-progress commit iteration to continue after termination. It is distinct from background-thread commit safety and the known pool shutdown problems.
Unbounded worker queues provide no backpressure, allowing queued work and memory usage to grow without limit.
Closing a strategy shuts down the factory-owned pool, which subsequent strategies reuse after rebalance despite its stopped workers and closed queues.
Setting worker shutdown flags before draining causes workers to abandon queued items and leave their offsets outstanding.
